- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 70), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is > 70 and true outcome is < 68, reduce forecast by 2–3% to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “1.00” patterns, model may be overfitting; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
